nciBridge.title: Net income and equity including non-controlling interests
nciBridge.content:
Net income (attributable) is the profit line shareholders of the parent actually receive; net income incl. NCI adds back the share earned by minority partners in consolidated subsidiaries and projects before that split. Total equity incl. NCI does the same for the balance sheet.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the mainland construction-investment/BOT-BT segment is run substantially through joint ventures and project companies with minority partners (including CSC Development, 830.HK), so consolidated NOPAT ties to the incl.-NCI line, not the attributable one — the DCF's FY0 NOPAT reconciles to NetIncomeInclNCI (~RMB9,005m FY2025: PBT 11,967.5 × (1-0.25)). NCI book value (~RMB3,742m at 2026-06-30) is then deducted once, in the equity bridge, to get from enterprise value to the value attributable to parent shareholders.

What to watch:

  • NCI's share of net income and equity growing faster than the attributable share, which would mean economic growth is increasingly accruing to minority partners
  • Equity incl. NCI diverging from attributable equity over time

perpetualsJv.title: Perpetual capital securities and JV/associate profit
perpetualsJv.content:
Perpetual capital securities are equity-classified instruments with no maturity date and discretionary distributions, but they carry a fixed coupon in substance and are debt-like economically. Share of JV/associate profit is the company's slice of earnings from joint ventures and associates that are equity-accounted rather than consolidated line-by-line.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: perpetuals stood at ~RMB5,570m at 2026-06-30 (distributions ~RMB334m in FY2025, sitting outside finance costs) and are deducted in the DCF's equity bridge alongside NCI, since they fund the balance sheet like debt even though they are booked in equity. JV/associate profit is material because the BOT-BT (build-operate-transfer) infrastructure investments in mainland China typically run through joint-venture project vehicles rather than wholly-owned subsidiaries.

What to watch:

  • Perpetuals growing as a source of balance-sheet funding (a lever to keep reported debt ratios lower)
  • JV profit share as a rising proportion of net income, meaning more of the growth engine sits off the main consolidated P&L lines

shareIssuance.title: Share issuance proceeds
shareIssuance.content:
Share issuance proceeds is cash raised from issuing new shares in the period.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the FY2025 bar is the ~RMB2.80bn placement completed that year — a one-off capital-raising event, not recurring financing or operating cash flow, and it diluted the share count used for EPS and the DCF's per-share value.

What to watch:

  • Whether proceeds funded growth capex/JV investment or simply shored up leverage ratios
  • Share count step-up in the period the placement settled

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For China State Construction International Holdings Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
